cands.name: Angela Gonzales-Torres

money.note: Individuals gave $481,409; PAC money $28,225; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democratic socialist and academic counselor at Pasadena City College's program for formerly incarcerated students, and program director for an affordable-housing project in Altadena. President of the Historic Highland Park Neighborhood Council 2023–25. Worked in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office. Defeated incumbent Jimmy Gomez in the 2026 CA-34 general election per Ballotpedia.

endorsements.text: Working Families Party, Justice Democrats PAC, Leaders We Deserve and Los Angeles Democratic Socialists of America endorsed her.
Our Revolution endorsed her, per Wikipedia.
Rep. Ro Khanna is quoted on her campaign site supporting her.

cands.gaps: Her sources disagree on whether she was born and raised in East Los Angeles or Highland Park, so only Los Angeles is stated. We found no date for when she came to California, because she appears to have lived here all her life. We found no detail on what she did in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office or when. She has held no legislative or executive office, so there is no governing record to report. We found no statements or actions from her on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, growth limits or land conservation, police pay and pensions, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. We found no foreign-government ties.

qual.background: Academic counselor at Pasadena City College supporting formerly incarcerated students, program director for a permanent affordable-housing project in Altadena, neighborhood council president 2023–25, and a past role in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office (specific duties not given). She has not held a legislative, executive, legal or prosecutorial office.
qual.why: Her work is in education counseling and housing programs, and her only elected post was a neighborhood council presidency, which is a civic body. Her Mayor's Office role is undocumented in the pages reviewed, so the score reflects limited governing experience.
qual.label: Her work is in education counseling and housing programs, and her only elected post was a neighborhood council presidency, which is a civic body. Her Mayor's Office role is undocumented in the pages reviewed, so the score reflects limited governing experience.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports a national moratorium on new data center construction until enforceable federal standards exist, and that local governments must keep the authority to say no to a data center. This is a national moratorium, not a statewide California ban.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site says she refuses corporate PAC and Super PAC money, that her campaign is powered by everyday Angelenos and not AIPAC, crypto or Big Tech, and that she backs abolishing Super PACs.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site calls for abolishing ICE, ending the mass deportation apparatus, and a pathway to citizenship for DACA recipients, TPS holders and essential workers.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says her Medicare for All plan would cover reproductive healthcare, and it criticizes the reversal of Roe v. Wade as a consequence of an unaccountable Supreme Court.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says she was born and raised in East Los Angeles and attended LAUSD schools, and her campaign site says she was born and raised in Highland Park and is a lifelong Angeleno.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Supports a national moratorium on new data center construction until Congress passes enforceable protections for workers, ratepayers and communities. Also calls for no tax abatements for data centers in heavily polluted communities, and for local governments to keep authority to say no.

Calls for repealing the Faircloth Amendment, which caps public housing growth, paired with direct construction funding and permanent affordability requirements, plus federal incentives for permanently affordable housing development.

cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 34th District since 2017, after serving in the California State Assembly (District 51) from 2012 to 2017. Former political director of United Nurses Associations of California and a former labor organizer. UCLA graduate with a Harvard Kennedy School master's in public policy.

controversies.text: Federal records show $22,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $213,629 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; $1,723,990 spent to help them by United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC, since 2021.
Missed 41 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (6.1%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 7, 2025-02-10 to 2025-02-13.

On Aug. 17, 2026, the House Ethics Committee opened an investigation into Gomez over alleged sexual misconduct, including a claim of sexual harassment and assault. Gomez says he did not violate House Ethics rules and that the interactions were consensual. As of Nov. 2, 2026, the investigation was ongoing, with no finding reported.

endorsements.text: 2026: U.S. Sen. Adam Schiff, the California Democratic Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and California Environmental Voters.
Wikipedia lists AIPAC, Democratic Majority for Israel and the AI-industry super PAC Leading the Future as endorsers.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and End Citizens United endorsed him in 2024, per his campaign site's news list.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position or action by Gomez on data centers, homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, gun laws, H-1B visas or school choice and teacher pay. Ballotpedia's page was cut off before its key votes and sponsored legislation sections. His campaign site's issues page was partly placeholder text and cut off. His birth city, his parents' arrival and when his family came to California were not stated. Campaign-site claims about bills he sponsored are his own statements, not checked against congress.gov.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: Gomez served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2017, including as Majority Whip. He has been a U.S. Representative since 2017 and sits on Ways and Means and the Intelligence Committee. Earlier he was a labor organizer and political director for a nurses' union.
qual.why: He has held legislative office for about 14 years, at both the state and federal level, which fits the high band for lawmaking, oversight and budgeting work.

clean-money.evidence: Gomez's campaign says he rejects corporate PAC money.

land-for-floridians.evidence: SFGATE, quoted by Ballotpedia, reported that Gomez supported a ban on large investors buying single-family homes.
